approach: Put the duty table, the due calculation, the runner seam and the standings in hestia.rs. Each duty is recorded as an ordinary check result in an `athena.hestia-sweep/1` record whose check id is the duty id, so the record shape does not change. That drops the earlier plan's change to crates/athena-data/src/records/throughput.rs and to crates/athena-cli/src/lib.rs. A duty's last run is the newest sweep that lists its check without `errored`. Landings since the last run are the landings (from `code_health::landings`) committed after that sweep's `at`. The drain start (`review_passes`), the landing hook (`code_health_after_landing`) and `athena hestia sweep` all go through one scheduler, `Athena::execute_duties`. It takes an occasion (drain start, landing or sweep), the landing times and `now`, all injected through a `DutyContext`. A drain or landing pass commits a sweep record only if a duty ran; the explicit sweep always commits. `StatusView.duties` holds `duty_standings` built from the same `duty_due`, so "overdue" means "the next sweep would run it". display.rs renders it. The doc gets section 13 with one table, and a test compares its ids and cadence text with `DUTIES`.

decisions.choice: Record a duty run as a check result named by the duty id in the existing `athena.hestia-sweep/1` record (`HestiaCheckResult { check: duty id, examined, count, errored }`). No new field, no new record kind.
decisions.reason: The sweep already lists every check that ran, with a count, and `validate`, `AnyRecord`, `canonical_path`, `check_record_file`, store.rs loading and `has_record_id` already cover it (records.rs:1131, 1232, 1333; throughput.rs:312-374). The existing `reading-rule-refusals` check id is already the reading-rule duty's record. This answers findings 2 and 5: crates/athena-data/src/records/throughput.rs and crates/athena-cli/src/lib.rs leave the plan, and records.rs only gains tests.

rejected.option: A `duties: Vec<DutyRun>` field on HestiaSweep with serde default
rejected.why: Edits throughput.rs and every HestiaSweep literal (hestia.rs, records.rs, cli lib.rs) to store what a check result already says.
Touches AnyRecord::validate, canonical_path, schema, store.rs loading, has_record_id and adds a record directory, for the same information.

rejected.option: Derive last run from CodeHealthBaseline or ThroughputReview timestamps
rejected.why: Only some duties leave such an artifact; the error-review, evidence-label and threshold duties leave nothing when they find nothing.

decisions.choice: Count "every N landings" from the landings committed after the duty's last successful sweep: `landing_times.iter().filter(|t| **t > last.at.as_second()).count()`. `landing_times` is `landings(&git, &head)` mapped to `Landing.at` (code_health.rs:392-427, commit time in epoch seconds). It sits in `DutyContext`, so tests inject it.
decisions.reason: No landing counter is stored, so the record needs no extra field. The same landing list the code-health baseline uses gives the count, and a second pass for the same landing sees zero new landings and runs nothing (steward.rs:105 and gh/landing.rs:984 both fire the hook for one landing). Seconds-level ties count as already seen.

rejected.option: Store the landing total in each duty run (for example in `examined`)

rejected.why: The brief states cadence as drain start, per landing or every N landings.

decisions.choice: The occasion decides which duties are eligible, and cadence decides whether an eligible one is due. Drain start: only DrainStart-cadence duties, always due. Landing: only EveryLanding and EveryLandings duties; due when never run or `since >= n`. Sweep (`athena hestia sweep`, and status): every duty; a DrainStart duty is due when never run or its last run is older than `DRAIN_DUTY_MAX_AGE_SECS` (24 h, an estimate); a landing duty as above. Status overdue = `duty_due` under the Sweep occasion.
decisions.reason: A drain start therefore runs exactly what it runs today (backfill, evidence labels), so drain tests do not suddenly run code-health, keep-rule or reading-rule on first drain. A landing runs the landing duties.

rejected.option: Every occasion runs every due duty
rejected.why: The first drain on any repository would run code-health, which writes a baseline and may queue structural-pass requests, changing drain-test fixtures and queues.

decisions.choice: The code-health duty (every landing) runs the existing `code_health_check` through a small `code_health_pass` helper. The design-review duty (every `REVIEW_EVERY` = 10 landings) reuses the `CheckReport` that pass cached in `AthenaDuties` (a `RefCell<Option<CheckReport>>`), or runs the pass itself if none is cached. It reports the review job if one was queued, else the landings since the baseline. `code_health_check` is not split or changed.
decisions.reason: The design review is already queued by the baseline logic inside `code_health_check` (code_health.rs:766-778). Running it twice per pass would give a second, misleading report, and splitting it would edit tested code. code_health.rs changes only in the hook (a delegate plus line helpers). It is still outside the listed files: `code_health_after_landing` is defined there, and the landing path (steward.rs:105, gh/landing.rs:984) calls it, so the sweep can own the landing cadence only by changing it. This answers finding 3.

rejected.option: Split `code_health_check` into structural and review halves
rejected.why: More edits in a tested function for no behavior gain.

rejected.option: Leave `code_health_after_landing` alone and have the sweep run code-health beside it
rejected.why: Two owners of one duty; the sweep could not claim a second pass runs none.

decisions.choice: A failed duty is recorded as an errored check result with the usual "the check failed to run" finding. It does not count as a run: the last run is the newest non-errored result, so the duty is due again at the next pass. Status shows `last_failed_at` when a failed attempt is newer than the last run.
decisions.reason: A failure then shows in `athena hestia last` and is retried, and nothing needs a new outcome type.

rejected.option: Treat a failed attempt as a run
rejected.why: A broken duty would look healthy and wait a whole cadence before retrying.

decisions.choice: Seam: `trait DutyRunner { fn run(&self, duty: &Duty, ui: &dyn Ui, now: Timestamp) -> Result<DutyOutput> }`. `Athena::hestia_sweep_duties(checks, ui, table: &[Duty], runner: &dyn DutyRunner, ctx: DutyContext) -> Result<Sweep>` executes the due duties, prints their lines, commits one sweep and returns it. Production uses `DUTIES`, `AthenaDuties` and `duty_context(occasion)`. The cadence test's double only logs which duty ids were asked to run.
decisions.reason: Due calculation, recording, the commit and reading it back are production code. The double holds no cadence logic.

rejected.option: Run the real six duties in the cadence test
rejected.why: They need model drivers and record fixtures, and they hide the cadence logic behind unrelated behavior.

decisions.choice: Duty cadences, written in both tables: error-review every drain start; evidence-labels every drain start; code-health every landing; design-review every 10 landings (`REVIEW_EVERY`); keep-rule every 10 landings; reading-rule-refusals every 5 landings. Ids: error-review, evidence-labels, code-health, design-review, keep-rule, reading-rule-refusals. The keep-rule duty runs `keep_rule(&records)` (status/planning.rs:242) and files a finding under check id `keep-rule` for a Breach or TurnOff verdict. Thresholds are untouched.
decisions.reason: All six duties have code to run today, so none needs to be invented. An id with no runner arm returns `Err("not yet automated")`, which shows as an errored check, so a future row cannot pass silently.

rejected.option: Weekly time cadence for the keep rule, as in hestia.md section 2 row 6
rejected.why: That row is the original estimate. The brief fixes the cadence kinds, and that table is not changed.

decisions.choice: Name a seam in every behavior demonstration, including criterion 5. The gate commands are demonstrated by running the real suite over the existing fixtures that drive the changed paths. These are `athena_in` in hestia.rs, the cli `Fixture` in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs and code_health_hooks.rs, and `set_up` in gh/after_merge_tests.rs. This answers finding 1.
decisions.reason: The brief requires a named seam for each behavior criterion.

decisions.choice: Update the cli files that render or exercise the changed paths: crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs (renders `athena status`; no listed file does) and crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (one existing assertion). Do not edit crates/athena-cli/src/lib.rs or throughput.rs. This answers findings 2, 4 and 5.
decisions.reason: A duties section in `athena status` needs one render call in `display::status` (display.rs:1159). main.rs only carries help text. The drain test at tests/drain.rs:4622 asserts the head does not move on a second drain, which stops being true once the drain-start duties record their last run.

rejected.option: Skip writing a record at drain start
rejected.why: Last run could not then be shown, and status would flag the drain-start duties overdue after 24 h.

steps: 1. In hestia.rs add the duty block under a new section header. `enum Cadence { DrainStart, EveryLanding, EveryLandings(u32) }` with `describe()` returning 'every drain start', 'every landing', or 'every N landings'. `#[derive(Clone, Copy)] struct Duty { id, name, cadence, runs_in }`. `pub const DUTIES: [Duty; 6]` in the order error-review, evidence-labels, code-health, design-review (`EveryLandings(crate::code_health::REVIEW_EVERY)`), keep-rule (10), reading-rule-refusals (5; its id is `READING_RULES_CHECK_ID`). `pub const DRAIN_DUTY_MAX_AGE_SECS: i64 = 86_400`. Add `enum Occasion { DrainStart, Landing, Sweep }` and `struct DutyContext { occasion, landing_times: Vec<i64>, now: Timestamp }`.

2. Add pure fns: `last_ok_run(sweeps, id) -> Option<Timestamp>` (newest sweep whose check list holds `id` with `errored == false`, by `at`); `last_failed_after(sweeps, id, ok) -> Option<Timestamp>`; `landings_since(times, last) -> usize`; `eligible(duty, occasion)`; `duty_due(duty, last, ctx) -> bool` implementing the decisions (never run is due; DrainStart cadence is due on the DrainStart occasion or older than the age limit; landing cadences are due when since >= n). Add `DutyStanding { id, name, cadence: String, runs_in, last_run: Option<Timestamp>, last_failed_at: Option<Timestamp>, next_due: String, overdue: bool }` (Serialize) and `duty_standings(table, sweeps, ctx)`; overdue equals `duty_due` under the Sweep occasion. `next_due` reads 'due now (never run)', 'at the next drain start (or after <last + 24 h>)', or 'after N more landing(s)'.

3. Add `struct DutyOutput { check: CheckOutput, lines: Vec<String> }`, `trait DutyRunner { fn run(&self, duty: &Duty, ui: &dyn Ui, now: Timestamp) -> Result<DutyOutput>; }` and the production `AthenaDuties<'a> { athena: &'a Athena, health: RefCell<Option<CheckReport>> }`. Its match on `duty.id`: error-review calls `error_review_backfill(ui)` and prints the existing backfill summary string; evidence-labels calls `derive_labels()` and the existing evidence-labels string (the two format strings moved out of `review_passes` into helpers, text unchanged); code-health runs `code_health_check(now)`, caches the report and returns the existing code-health lines (helpers added in code_health.rs); design-review reuses the cached report or runs the check, and reports the queued review job or the landings since the baseline; keep-rule calls `keep_rule(&records)` and files a finding for a Breach or TurnOff verdict; reading-rule-refusals runs `self.athena.reading_rules_check(head).run(now)`. Any other id returns `Err` 'not yet automated'.

4. Factor the per-check body of `run_sweep` (hestia.rs:151-191) into `settle(check_id, outcome) -> (CheckResult, Vec<Finding>)`, used by `run_sweep` and the duty pass. Add `Athena::duty_context(occasion) -> Result<DutyContext>` (landing times from `crate::code_health::landings(&self.git, &head)?`, mapped to `.at`; `now = crate::now()`). Add `Athena::execute_duties(table, runner, ctx, ui) -> Result<DutyReport { results, findings, lines }>`: it loads sweeps with `Records::load_current` as `status()` does, and for each eligible and due duty in table order runs it through the runner, settles the result and collects its lines (an `Err` becomes an errored result plus the line `hestia     <id>: could not run: <error>`).

5. Change `commit_sweep(checks, duties: DutyReport, now)` to merge the duty results and findings into the swept checks before `validate` (replacing the `reading_rules: bool` argument). `hestia_sweep(checks)` passes an empty report and `crate::now()`. Add `Athena::hestia_sweep_duties(checks, ui, table, runner, ctx) -> Result<Sweep>` (execute, print the lines, commit with `ctx.now`) and `Athena::run_due_duties(occasion, ui) -> Vec<String>` (execute with `DUTIES` and `AthenaDuties`, commit only when at least one duty ran, return the lines; a commit error is returned as a line). Rework `review_passes` to return `run_due_duties(DrainStart)` lines followed by the unchanged spec and throughput lines (moved into `extra_review_passes`). Rework `hestia_sweep_with` to run the Sweep-occasion duties, then `extra_review_passes`, then the build measurement, then commit once.

6. In code_health.rs make `code_health_after_landing` call `self.run_due_duties(Occasion::Landing, ui)` and print each line. Add small helpers for the existing line texts (:720-742) that the code-health and design-review duties use. `code_health_check` is untouched. Update the hestia.rs module header (lines 1-82) to name the sweep as the owner of the duties and point to hestia.md section 13.

7. In status.rs add `pub duties: Vec<crate::hestia::DutyStanding>` to `StatusView` with a doc comment. In `status()`, build it with `duty_standings(&DUTIES, &records.hestia_sweeps, ctx)`, where ctx has the Sweep occasion, the landing times from `landings(&self.git, &head)` (empty if that fails) and `crate::now()`. Add the criterion 2 tests. In display.rs add the duties section after the reading-rules and throughput lines, one line per duty with an OVERDUE mark. In main.rs update the two help texts.

8. Write docs/design/hestia.md section 13 'Recurring duties': one table with the six rows (id, duty, owner 'Hestia's sweep', cadence text exactly as `Cadence::describe`, where it runs). Add short text on the three occasions (drain start, landing, `athena hestia sweep`), how a run is recorded (a check result named by the duty id), the overdue rule (24 h, an estimate, for drain-start duties; landings counted after the last run), and that the throughput and spec passes are not duties. Add the `the_duty_table_matches_the_design_doc` test and the criterion 1 test in hestia.rs.

9. Add the records.rs tests (criterion 7). Update the existing tests listed in dependents: hestia.rs 3228 and 5020, and the last assertion of the second-drain test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs. Add the CHANGELOG.md entry under Unreleased / Added.

10. Run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` over the workspace, and also `cargo test -p athena-core`, `-p athena-data` and `-p athena-cli`, which call the changed paths.

risks.risk: Every drain start and every landing now commits a small sweep record on the records branch (the two drain-start duties run each drain; code-health runs each landing). An existing test that asserts the head does not move would fail.
risks.mitigation: A drain or landing pass commits only if a duty ran, and the explicit sweep always commits. The one known assertion (tests/drain.rs:4622) is updated in step 9. The full `cargo test --locked` is the gate and finds any other. Last run cannot be shown without a record, so this cost is accepted.

risks.risk: Landing time is the commit time (`%ct`) compared with the sweep's local `at`, so a host clock ahead of the local clock could make a new landing look older than the last run and hide it from the count.
risks.mitigation: This is the same landings list the code-health baseline uses. The test injects times, and the doc and changelog state the rule. A missed count only delays an every-N duty to a later landing; it never blocks work (Hestia never gates).

risks.risk: The first sweep, or the first landing on an old repository, runs several duties at once (code-health writes the baseline, keep-rule and reading-rule read records).
risks.mitigation: Code-health keeps its first-baseline behavior (code_health.rs:766-770, covered by tests at 1421-1474). The design-review duty reuses the code-health report in the same pass. The drain-start occasion runs only the two drain-start duties, so drain tests do not gain these runs.

risks.risk: The 24 h limit for drain-start duties is a guess and flags an idle repository as overdue.
risks.mitigation: It is the named constant `DRAIN_DUTY_MAX_AGE_SECS`, labeled an estimate in the table text and the changelog, and status says 'at the next drain start'. It gates nothing.

risks.risk: Status reads records through `load_current` while `last_sweep` uses `Records::load(head)`, so the two could disagree on a deployed repository.
risks.mitigation: The duty pass reads last runs with `Records::load_current(&git, &head, &records_worktree(state.root()))`, the call `status()` makes and `reading_rules_check` already makes (hestia.rs:2786), so scheduler and status agree. The criterion 2 test commits a sweep with `commit_in_tree` and reads it through `status()`.

risks.risk: hestia.rs is about 288 KB and grows, and the code-health file-size check may queue a structural pass for it.
risks.mitigation: The brief names hestia.rs as the home of the table and the tests. The duty code is one contiguous block under its own section header, so a later split into a submodule is a pure move.

demonstrations.method: A unit test `a_sweep_runs_each_due_duty_records_the_last_run_and_a_second_sweep_runs_none` in hestia.rs `mod tests`. The fixture is `athena_in(dir, state)`. The table holds three test duties: A DrainStart, B EveryLanding, C EveryLandings(3). A `CountingRunner` logs the ids it is asked to run. The test calls `athena.hestia_sweep_duties(&[], &Quiet, &table, &runner, ctx)` with these contexts: (1) Sweep, no landings, time T: A, B and C all run. (2) Sweep, same landings, T+1: none run. (3) Sweep, one landing at T+2, now T+3: B only. (4) Sweep, landings T+2, T+4, T+5, now T+6: B and C. (5) the same landings, T+7: none. (6) DrainStart occasion: A only. (7) Landing occasion with one more landing: B only. (8) Sweep at T+25 h: A only, by age. After each sweep the test reads `athena.last_sweep()` and checks its check ids equal the ids the runner was asked for, so the first holds three checks and the second none.
demonstrations.observes: The runner's call log matches each expectation above. After sweep 1 the committed record lists A, B and C as non-errored checks. After sweep 2 the committed record lists no checks. The last-run times come from the committed records read back through `Athena::last_sweep`.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the sweep ignored cadence, sweep 2 would call all three duties. If it did not record the check ids, `last_sweep().checks` would be empty and sweep 2 would re-run everything. If the landing count were wrong, steps 3, 4 and 7 would run the wrong duties.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry `Athena::hestia_sweep_duties` (added by step 5). Fixture `athena_in` exists (hestia.rs:2984). The double `CountingRunner` implements the production trait `DutyRunner` (added by step 3) and only records ids. Landing times and `now` are injected through `DutyContext`, so no landed commits and no clock are needed.
